name: @typecrate/provider
description: Rust-native private model provider for the TypeCrate scope: the vault-artifact credential/endpoint substrate and the OpenAI-compatible model clients ported from @agentic/provider.
#identity: npm identity for the Rust crate at packages/typecrate/provider. Crate name == npm name with @ dropped and / replaced by - (rust/README.md name mapping): @typecrate/provider <-> typecrate-provider <-> `use typecrate_provider::...`. The crate version and this version line are pinned together and src/lib.rs::version_matches_the_npm_line reads THIS file and asserts they agree. private: true because the artifact is a cargo build inside this repo, not a published package yet.
#layout: Rust-first, and native-runnable since the `[[bin]]` pass: Cargo.toml is a standalone Cargo workspace (its own explicit [workspace] boundary, because the root workspace globs only rust/crates/* and without the boundary cargo says 'current package believes it's in a workspace when it's not'), with one rlib target PLUS `[[bin]] name = "typecrate-provider-server"` (path src/bin/server.rs). THE CRATE NOW OWNS A LISTENER OF ITS OWN: `start:server` and a pushed payload both bind 8800 in THIS crate's process. `endpoint/provider/provider-route.rs` is the ALTERNATIVE host, not the only one - packages/typecrate/services links the rlib, discovers that route file and serves the four routes on its own gateway listener, and in THAT host 8800 is only the port the mount is declared for. The two hosts are never stacked: the bin depends one-way on the lib (src/bin/server.rs header), so an embedder that runs the route file never starts this executable. Artifacts land in the repo-root .rust/target because ../../../.cargo/config.toml sets target-dir; cargo picks that config up by walking up from this directory. The crate is excluded from the root workspace, so nothing here uses `.workspace = true` inheritance: edition/rust-version/version/license/publish, [lints] and [profile.release] are all restated literally. The npm layer is no longer cargo-only: scripts/*.ts drive deploys (see #deploy, #ts).
#rust: check / test / lint / lint:strict / build / build:server / start:server are plain cargo on the toolchain pinned by rust-toolchain.toml (1.99.1). Every one of them carries --locked (see #locked); --offline is NOT part of any script, exactly as in packages/typecrate/harness and packages/typecrate/services - it is added per invocation on a host with no registry access, where the graph in Cargo.lock IS the build. The old claim that NO verb needs a vite-node pre-step is now true of the CARGO verbs only: deploy:endpoint / start:modal / start:daytona are vite-node scripts (root-hoisted, so no build step, and never raw node - root AGENTS.md runner policy), and the only cargo they run is the client's own cargoReleaseBin recipe (see #deploy). Artifacts land in the repo-root .rust/target (see #layout).
#deploy: What deploy:endpoint / start:modal / start:daytona push, and how the payload stays ANONYMOUS. The release ELF from `build:server` and the vault artifact config/vault/generated/agentic-provider.json are packed as ONE flat tar.gz with exactly two members - `typecrate-provider-server` mode 0755 (the file the container execs) and `agentic-provider.json` mode 0644 (its credentials) - and POSTed with NO `x-runtime-profile` header, i.e. the container's anonymous config-only profile (services/daytona/sandbox/runtime-server/src/contract.rs). The config carries only runCmd `./typecrate-provider-server`, port 8800, artifactPath, probeTimeoutSec 120, stopSignal SIGTERM and env { TYPECRATE_PROVIDER_VAULT_PATH: ./agentic-provider.json, RUST_LOG: info }; probePath is deliberately ABSENT, because its absence means readiness is a bare TCP connect and the container then needs NO knowledge of what it is running. Anonymity cuts both ways, and this is the contract the operator deploys against: the container does not authenticate the CALLER (anyone who knows the API can use it - authentication is the payload's own business, which is why the vault document rides INSIDE the bundle), and no secret may go into config.env, because the container's GET /status echoes the posted config verbatim to a caller that presented no secret (the client's own configNotes flag credential-shaped env keys). The endpoint is an ARGUMENT, never a package constant: --endpoint/positional > TYPECRATE_PROVIDER_ENDPOINT > @config/vault modalContainer, because the Modal box this repo deploys to is occupied by another workload and a second box has its own https://<source>--<BOX_LABEL>.modal.run URL (README 'Getting a dedicated box'). The deploy client is SHARED with nexus - @services/daytona/sandbox's runtime-deploy.ts (packagePayload/cargoReleaseBin/deployPayload/probeEndpoint/resolveSlot/teardown, every side effect injected) - so this package declares a workload, it does not re-implement the contract, and the busy-slot policy (DELETE /, or DELETE /sandbox to replace the CONTAINER on a Modal box) is decided from the endpoint's own /health, never from a flag.
#locked: build/check/test/clippy run with --locked: Cargo.lock is committed for this standalone workspace, so the dependency graph can never be silently re-resolved by an npm script. Regenerate deliberately with `cargo generate-lockfile` (online) and commit it - never as a side effect of a script. `fmt`/`fmt:check` take no lock part. There is no vendored registry in this repo, so every dependency has to be one the sibling typecrate lockfiles already resolve (packages/typecrate/{harness,services}/Cargo.lock): axum and reqwest are declared now (the route layer needs them) at exactly those shared versions, and a new dependency needs an online lockfile refresh before it can build here.
#lint-vs-lint-strict: `lint` is what root `turbo run test` executes (turbo test dependsOn lint), so it must not deny warnings; `lint:strict` is the -D warnings gate used by verify and CI. This mirrors packages/typecrate/services exactly; packages/typecrate/harness predates the split and has lint deny warnings on its own.
#scope: PORTED TODAY (the whole port list, and src/lib.rs's module table is the maintained map): `vault.rs` the vault artifact loader (config/vault/generated/<scope>.json, the document `yarn workspace @config/vault export -- --consumer agentic-provider` writes; nothing here regenerates it), `transport.rs` the outbound OpenAI-compatible substrate (endpoints/credential pools, retry/rotation, JSON + SSE paths), `sse.rs` the frame codec, `error.rs` the failure taxonomy and error-frame wire shape, `pricing.rs`, `accounting.rs` the lifetime counters, `client.rs` the declarative model client, `config/provider/**/*.json` the served row table (compiled by `build.rs` into `clients.rs`), `registry.rs` rows+vault, and `serve.rs` the four service routes (chat completions, responses, models, stats) plus `endpoint/provider/provider-route.rs` for the services mount. STILL NOT PORTED, named in src/lib.rs: the /stats HTML dashboard and its cross-process buffer (this crate publishes the same projection as JSON), the Daytona GPU-sandbox substrate, and the Lightning Chat-to-Responses adapter (the TypeScript does not register those clients, so their absence IS the parity behaviour).
#artifact: The loader never reads an environment variable and never defaults a path, so NOTHING here regenerates or requires the artifact: run `yarn workspace @config/vault export -- --consumer agentic-provider` to produce config/vault/generated/agentic-provider.json (git-ignored, absent on a fresh clone). When it is missing, the artifact-gated tests do NOT pass silently: the test that ran zero assertions prints its own name, the words NOT CHECKED, the artifact path, the regeneration command and the exact re-run (tests/registry.rs ::artifact). cargo test captures a PASSING test's stderr, so `--nocapture` is what surfaces that line - knowledge.md 'Known limitations' records the requirement, which is why this is louder than the config/vault/src/vault/artifact.test.ts analogue that puts the reason in the test title. Nothing fabricates a value. THE DEPLOY VERBS HAVE THE SAME RULE AND A DIFFERENT OUTCOME: scripts/deploy-endpoint.ts refuses to ship at all when that file is absent (a container that boots with no credentials is a deploy that looks like it worked), and its error text carries the same regeneration command.

scripts.#build:server: The one cargo verb that produces the DEPLOYABLE artifact, and the recipe scripts/deploy-endpoint.ts runs through the shared client's cargoReleaseBin (services/daytona/sandbox/runtime-deploy.ts:931-944: the same `build --release --locked -p <pkg> --message-format=json`; the client adds `--bin` nowhere, so `cargo build -p` builds the bin as a package target). --message-format=json is deliberate: the NDJSON `executable` field is the only reliable locator, because the target dir is not guessable (the repo-root .cargo/config.toml sets it to .rust/target). Artifact: <repo-root>/.rust/target/release/typecrate-provider-server - NOT provider/target/.
scripts.#start:server: The crate's own listener, natively: no typecrate-services router, no Node, no route discovery. The trailing `--` is cargo's separator, so everything after it reaches the bin: `yarn workspace @typecrate/provider start:server -- --port 0`. Flags, environment, exit codes and the SIGTERM drain: src/bin/server.rs HELP and README 'Running it natively'.
scripts.#deploy-verbs: Three verbs, all thin drivers over the SHARED client @services/daytona/sandbox (the runtime-contract client nexus uses too): deploy:endpoint takes the URL as an argument, start:modal supplies the vault's box URL as the LAST-resort default (positional/--endpoint > TYPECRATE_PROVIDER_ENDPOINT > @config/vault modalContainer, because this repo's box is occupied by another workload), start:daytona mints a sandbox of its own and needs no URL at all. `--out <path>` writes the bundle without deploying; `--dry-run` is fully offline (no probe, no POST, no cargo - the artifact must already exist, so run build:server first). Payload and anonymity contract: #deploy.
scripts.#ts: The TypeScript surface is scripts/*.ts ONLY: `typecheck` runs tsc --noEmit against tsconfig.json (extends the root config, whose exclude already drops **/*.test.ts), and `test:scripts` runs vitest over the colocated script tests, which inject every side effect - no network, no cargo, no Daytona/Modal calls. Both NEED the monorepo: the root tsconfig and the workspace packages they import (@config/vault, @services/daytona) live outside this repository, which is exactly why .github/workflows/ci.yml runs cargo and nothing else. `test` stays cargo, which is what turbo orchestrates.
scripts.verify: npm run fmt:check && npm run lint:strict && npm run test && npm run build

#dependencies: scripts/start-modal.ts reads the Modal box URL from @config/vault, and all three verbs drive the deploy through @services/daytona/sandbox (createSandbox + the runtime-deploy client); house convention is "*" + TS sources resolved through the workspace symlink (no build step, no lockfile entry needed for a private workspace package). Same shape as packages/typecrate/nexus/package.json:38-42. These are RUNTIME-TIME deps of the vite-node scripts only - `cargo test` never imports them, which is what keeps the CI note in .github/workflows/ci.yml honest.
